frictions.description: Playwright Chromium headless shell required manual installation of system library dependencies (libnspr4, libnss3, etc.) via .deb download and extraction.
frictions.resolution: Used pre-extracted libraries at /tmp/chromium-libs/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/ with LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

blockers.description: QEMU Wasm Worker thread consistently fails to allocate 2300MB WebAssembly linear memory in any Chrome headless mode (headless shell, --headless=new, direct CDP). V8 internal 'Array buffer allocation failed' error. Manual Wasm memory allocation succeeds in the main thread (new WebAssembly.Memory({initial: 37120, shared: true}) works), but the allocation fails in the Worker thread context. System has 9GB available RAM. Tried Chrome with --js-flags='--max-old-space-size=8192 --wasm-max-mem-pages=65536', --enable-features=WebAssembly,SharedArrayBuffer — all failed. This is likely a Chrome headless Worker memory limit that differs from the main thread limit.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Tried multiple Chrome launch configurations (headless shell, headless=new, direct CDP, various js-flags, feature flags). All fail identically. The issue is specific to Worker thread Wasm memory allocation in this environment.

summary: Tested 15 input/interaction assertions plus VAL-CROSS-001. All code inspection and unit tests pass — scancode mappings correct, focus gating works, blur releases keys, mouse deltas tracked. Button state machine verified live in browser (Start→disabled, Reboot→enabled after Start click). All 15 live verification tests blocked by QEMU Wasm Worker memory allocation failure in headless Chrome.
